steps.message:
I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Today is Saturday, October 24, 2026. Submissions close six days from today, on Friday, at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Today is 2026-10-24 (Saturday). +6 days = 2026-10-30 (Friday). Deadline: 23:59 PDT (UTC-7, as US DST ends Nov 1).  
This is 2026-10-31 06:59 UTC. Madrid (CET, UTC+1 after DST ended Oct 25) is 8h ahead: 07:59 on 2026-10-31.  
ANSWER: 2026-10-31 07:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Today is Friday, October 30, 2026. The form closes this coming Monday at 10:00 AM Los Angeles time."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The deadline is Monday, Nov 2 2026 at 10:00 LA time (PST, UTC-8). Madrid uses CET (UTC+1) in November, a 9-hour difference.  
ANSWER: 2026-11-02 19:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The hackathon starts Saturday, October 24, 2026 at 18:00 Madrid time and lasts exactly 48 hours."
When is the end of the hackathon in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The hackathon starts at 18:00 CEST (UTC+2) on 2026-10-24, or 16:00 UTC. Exactly 48 hours later is 16:00 UTC on 2026-10-26. DST ends on Sunday 2026-10-25 (last Sunday in October), so Madrid is on CET (UTC+1) by the 26th, making the local time 17:00.  
ANSWER: 2026-10-26 17:00 (24-hour clock, my local time)

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The final round starts October 26, 2026 at 10:00 AM PT; submissions close exactly 72 hours later."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Start: Oct 26 2026 10:00 PDT (UTC-7) = 17:00 UTC.  
+72 h = Oct 29 2026 17:00 UTC.  
Madrid on that date uses CET (UTC+1; DST ended Oct 25).  
Thus local time is 18:00.  
ANSWER: 2026-10-29 18:00 (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close October 31, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET. Results are announced exactly 36 hours after submissions close."
When is the results announcement in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Deadline (Unix timestamp, seconds): 1791788340."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The Unix timestamp 1791788340 equals 2026-10-12 06:59:00 UTC (calculated via total days since 1970-01-01 accounting for 14 leap years in the interval, day-of-year 285 = Oct 12 in non-leap 2026, and exact remainder seconds). Tokyo is UTC+9 with no DST.  
ANSWER: 2026-10-12 15:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Deadline: 2026-10-25T02:30:00Z."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The given deadline is 02:30 UTC on 2026-10-25. Madrid observes CEST (UTC+2) until 03:00 local on the last Sunday of October (which falls on 2026-10-25), when clocks fall back to CET (UTC+1). Since 02:30 UTC occurs after the 01:00 UTC transition point, the equivalent local time is 03:30 CET on the same date.  
ANSWER: 2026-10-25 03:30

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close at 11:59 PM Pacific Time on the last Sunday of October 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The last Sunday of Oct 2026 is the 25th (calculated from Jan 1 2026 being Thursday; Oct 1 is also Thursday). This deadline is 23:59 PDT (UTC-7, as US DST ends Nov 1). That converts to 06:59 UTC on Oct 26, or 07:59 CET (UTC+1) in Madrid (post-DST change at 03:00 local on Oct 25).  
ANSWER: 2026-10-26 07:59

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Deadline: 12:00 noon Eastern Time on the day the US ends daylight saving time in 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The US ends DST on the first Sunday in November. In 2026 this is November 1 (confirmed via day-of-week shift from known 2024 date of Nov 3). Noon ET on that date is after the 2 a.m. clock change, so it is EST (UTC-5). Lima uses UTC-5 year-round with no DST observed.  
ANSWER: 2026-11-01 12:00

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Deadline: December 31, 2026, 24:00 AoE."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Tokyo is UTC+9; AoE is UTC-12 (difference: +21 h).  
Dec 31 24:00 AoE = Jan 1 00:00 (UTC-12) = Jan 1 21:00 (Tokyo).  
ANSWER: 2027-01-01 21:00

I live in Madrid, Spain, but that week I'm traveling in New York, USA, and I need New York time. A contest page says: "The deadline is 5:00 PM Sydney time on October 5, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Sydney is on AEDT (UTC+11) on this date (DST started Oct 4). 17:00 AEDT = 06:00 UTC. NY is on EDT (UTC-4) in October. 06:00 UTC = 02:00 EDT same day.  
ANSWER: 2026-10-05 02:00
